blocks.text: No naira can lawfully leave the Federation Account until 469 people in Abuja have voted to release it. That single fact — control of the purse — is why the legislature matters more than its quiet chambers suggest.

blocks.markdown: The **legislature** is the organ of government that makes, amends and repeals the law. It is known by different names: the National Assembly in Nigeria, Parliament in Britain, Congress in the United States, and a House of Assembly at Nigerian state level.

items: **Law making** — enacting, amending and repealing statutes; this is its primary function.
**Control of public finance** — approving taxation and passing the Appropriation Act, without which no money may be withdrawn from the Federation Account.
**Oversight of the executive** — summoning officials, holding investigative hearings and questioning ministers.
**Representation** — voicing the interests and grievances of constituents.
**Constitutional amendment** — altering the Constitution by the prescribed special majority.
**Confirmation of appointments** — screening nominees for ministerial, ambassadorial, judicial and commission posts.
**Removal of officials** — impeaching the President or Vice-President for gross misconduct.
**Ratification of treaties** — giving domestic legal effect to international agreements.
**Quasi-judicial functions** — punishing contempt of the House and conducting investigations.
**Deliberative and educative functions** — debating national issues publicly and so informing citizens.

blocks.title: Unicameral and bicameral legislatures
blocks.text: A UNICAMERAL legislature has one chamber; a BICAMERAL legislature has two. Federations are almost always bicameral because the second chamber represents the component units equally, offsetting the population-based first chamber. Nigeria's National Assembly is bicameral; Ghana's Parliament is unicameral.

blocks.caption: Nigeria's National Assembly under the 1999 Constitution. Members of both chambers serve four-year terms

blocks.markdown:
### Arguments for and against a second chamber

**For**: it checks hasty or ill-considered legislation; it gives the component units of a federation equal representation; it allows more thorough scrutiny of bills; and it provides a place for experienced elder statesmen.

**Against**: it is expensive to maintain; it slows law making; it duplicates work already done in the first chamber; and where both chambers are controlled by the same party the check may be more apparent than real.

blocks.title: How a bill becomes law in Nigeria
blocks.prompt: Trace an executive bill from introduction to enactment, and state what happens if the President refuses assent.

steps.text: First reading: the short title of the bill is read and it is formally introduced. There is no debate at this stage.
Second reading: members debate the general principles and merits of the bill. If it survives the vote, it proceeds.
Committee stage: the relevant standing committee examines the bill clause by clause, holds a public hearing, takes memoranda and proposes amendments.
Report and third reading: the committee reports back, the amended bill is considered and then read a third time and passed by that chamber.
The bill goes through the same stages in the other chamber. If the two versions differ, a joint conference committee harmonises them and both chambers adopt the harmonised version.
The clean copy is transmitted to the President for assent. Once he signs, the bill becomes an Act of the National Assembly.
If the President withholds assent, the National Assembly may pass the bill again by a two-thirds majority of each chamber, and it then becomes law without his signature.

blocks.answer: First reading, second reading, committee stage, report and third reading, the same stages in the other chamber, harmonisation if needed, then presidential assent — or a two-thirds override in both chambers if assent is withheld

blocks.title: Get the Nigerian numbers right
blocks.text: Senate 109, House of Representatives 360, four-year terms. The Senate's 109 is 3 from each of 36 states, which is 108, plus 1 for the Federal Capital Territory. Being able to explain where the odd number comes from shows the examiner you understand the principle of equal state representation.

points: The legislature makes, amends and repeals law, and controls public finance through the Appropriation Act.
It also represents constituents, oversees the executive, confirms appointments, amends the Constitution and can impeach the President.
A unicameral legislature has one chamber; a bicameral legislature has two, which suits a federation.
Nigeria's National Assembly consists of a 109-member Senate and a 360-member House of Representatives, both serving four-year terms.
A bill passes three readings and a committee stage in each chamber before going to the President for assent.
A withheld assent can be overridden by a two-thirds majority of each chamber.
